question: How did two landslides make one giant tsunami?
answer: The first slide plunged into the bay and raised a wave. The second, farther away, struck the glacier and made no new wave; it added its force to the first. Together the two slides summed their destructive power into one bigger tsunami.
move: A push that lands on a passing wave adds to it: two slides, one bigger tsunami.
